recbqsYSV8FGvCA28.Bio: Kyle Denton is a community herbalist and medicine maker from Wisconsin who founded Tippecanoe Herbs with his wife Serena Marinelli in 2015. From their Milwaukee apothecary they craft small batch remedies from locally harvested and organic herbs, working from a bio terrain philosophy that blends Ayurveda with Western herbalism. He also runs Root Radical Herbal Academy, has taught for over a decade through his annual three season class and his Milwaukee herb walks, and sees clients as the Tuning Herbalist, using tuning forks to read the biofield. His Substack and podcast, Resonature, explore the interval between vital herbalism, biofield tuning and cosmology.
recbqsYSV8FGvCA28.Name: Kyle Denton
recbqsYSV8FGvCA28.Role: Community herbalist, founder of Tippecanoe Herbs

fields.Core Themes JSON: [{"title": "The Tongue as the Body's Early Warning Map", "body": "Drawing on fifteen years of chairside work, Kyle describes the tongue as a reflex map much like the ear or the foot, with the tip tied to the heart and the conscious mind that Chinese medicine calls the shen, the sides to the lungs, liver and spleen, and the back to the kidneys and bladder. He reads scalloped edges as dampness, a trembling tongue as wind, a pointed one as fire, and a carmine pink body as the healthy baseline, and he says the tongue often shows a change days before the body feels it, while Chance wonders whether a part that stays hidden is simply freer to change."}, {"title": "Brushing and Scraping as Rituals of Self Worth", "body": "Kyle tells his clients to start with a tongue scraper, or simply the back of a spoon, and to scrape seven times each morning, because in his view the act itself sends a signal to the organs that things are getting cleaner. The deeper point is the mindset behind the habit: the same thirty seconds at the sink can either rub the stress of the inbox into the body or become a moment of Venusian pleasure, of welcoming yourself in the mirror rather than examining yourself, and of affirming that you are worthy of taking care of yourself."}, {"title": "Teeth as Living Tissue Shaped From Within", "body": "Rather than leaning on tooth to organ charts, which Kyle worries can trigger a victim fear response, he returns to the simple things: teeth are a living mineral lattice of enamel over spongy dentin over the pulp, fed by fluid moving through tiny channels. Kyle says teeth are mineralized from the inside out, steered by an endocrine system that holds minerals back under fight or flight, and he reads Weston A. Price as a lesson in whole living rather than butter and fish oil. Chance adds that healing is not fixing brokenness but expressing an innate wholeness that missing teeth never touch."}, {"title": "Meeting the Dentist in Good Faith", "body": "Kyle has watched dentistry from the corporate chain to a three generation family practice under his mentor Dr. Funke, and he argues that many dentists genuinely want to help while insurance underwriters pull the strings. His approach is to call ahead about fluoride policies, treat every recommendation as an offer on the table, ask to see the spot on the X-ray, and propose rechecking a small problem in a few months. He suggests kava kava for the diplomacy of speaking up, and Chance adds that patients should never feel pressured into a procedure that is clearly not an emergency."}, {"title": "Black Walnut, Iodine and Doubts About Receptors", "body": "Kyle's plant of the season is the black walnut, Juglans nigra, the nut of Jupiter whose green hulls blacken as they oxidize, a change he credits to iodine. Kyle says iodine can help reverse demineralization and decay by working through the thyroid, and he notes that fluorine and chlorine, the halogens added to municipal water, share iodine's group on the periodic table. That leads the pair to question the cell receptor model itself, raising the staining and fixing steps of electron microscopy and Howard Hillman's argument that there is simply not enough room on a cell for every receptor claimed."}]
fields.Intro Paragraph 1: Master herbalist Kyle Denton returns to InnerVerse to explore holistic oral health, dental herbalism, and a terrain perspective on teeth, tongues, and mineralization. Drawing on 15 years working in the dental field, the man behind Tippecanoe Herbs brings a whole-body approach to caring for our mouths. What might your tongue reveal about your body? Why does Kyle approach tooth mineralization from the inside out? And what happens when daily hygiene becomes an opportunity for mental cleansing, too?
fields.Intro Paragraph 2: We explore traditional tongue assessment, tongue scraping, nutrition, stress, and the connections Kyle draws between dental health and the endocrine system. Along the way, we discuss biofield tuning, kava, black walnut, navigating dental anxiety, and choosing a dentist you can communicate with. It’s a conversation about taking care of ourselves from a place of innate wholeness.

fields.Plus Core Themes JSON: [{"title": "Black Walnut, Juglone and the Terrain", "body": "Kyle Denton calls black walnut the Juggalo of nature, an unwanted tree whose iodine rich green hull he credits with shifting the terrain so parasites lose their job rather than causing disease. He questions the Roman era warning that nothing grows beneath a walnut, pointing to raspberries and burdock thriving under his own tree and to a University of Washington study where juglone stunted growth in a Petri dish but changed nothing in real soil, which suggests the shade of a big canopy is the simpler culprit. He harvests leaves before the summer solstice for tooth powder and double gloves before hulling."}, {"title": "The Thyroid, the Throat and the Voice", "body": "Kyle wonders aloud whether iodine is even a thing, preferring to describe it as a valence or charge the thyroid craves, and he works with a three plant formula from Matthew Wood pairing ashwagandha, blue flag iris and black walnut hull. Chance maps thyroid patterns onto the biofield, placing overactive conflict about being unheard on the right side of the throat and held back speech on the left, and suggests a weighted fork paired with a matching mantra. Kyle links throat and root as above, so below, noting that kava kava can defuse pent up charge so old stuff can finally let go."}, {"title": "Fluoride, Nano and the Toothpaste Pitch", "body": "Kyle concedes that topical fluoride makes a harder tooth surface but asks whether harder means better, since a rigid surface may fracture and teeth, in his view, act as piezoelectric bio resonators that need to flex, a point Chance compares to martial arts. He calls the idea that swallowed fluoride knows to travel only to the teeth nonsense, and he distrusts nano hydroxyapatite for the same reason, choosing a non nano version ground from cow bone. His base tooth powder blends calcium carbonate, a little baking soda, bentonite clay and herbs matched to the person, like yarrow for bleeding gums or clove for bad breath."}, {"title": "Clove, Eugenol and the Filling That Lasted", "body": "Kyle sucks on a clove twice a day, rolling it around his teeth like a tongue assisted toothpick for about ten minutes, and explains that clove eases a toothache by flooding the area with blood flow and saliva. Working across from a veterans hospital, he saw intermediate restorative material fillings placed in the Vietnam era still sound 30 to 40 years later, which he credits to eugenol, the oil of clove, encouraging secondary dentin. Chance contrasts a fix it once military mindset with a model built on repeat visits, and Kyle urges listeners to ask their dentist to try a conservative temporary filling first."}, {"title": "Gum Disease as a Mineral Question", "body": "With 48 percent of Americans showing some form of gum disease, Kyle asks whether half the country really brushes wrong, citing periodontology textbooks to argue the problem is often metabolic, with the spongy alveolar bone surrendering minerals to the arms and legs. He offers a brushing tip, switching hands at the midline, and reads jaw tension as stress between thought and emotion. For daily minerals he favors fat soluble nutrition from good butter and raw milk alongside nutritive infusions of silica rich oat straw and nettles, plants he treats as teachers that help the body use the minerals it already has."}]

If you're too rigid, you break. You got to be able to be more wobbly.", "author": "Chance Garton", "portrait": "https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/5987d897cf81e0278ec5322e/aa717e55-9487-4255-a7df-3f8ef10940c4/Chance+Garton+Patreon+Portrait.png?content-type=image%2Fpng"}, {"text": "When you're about to have a conversation with somebody new in Japanese culture, you would swish your mouth out, and you might even spit it out with some tea.", "author": "Kyle Denton", "portrait": "https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/5987d897cf81e0278ec5322e/3bfe296c-3dcd-4af6-bc2e-26466a87ec04/KYLE-DENTON.png?content-type=image%2Fpng"}, {"text": "Have a little mantra that when I speak, I'm heard, and when I'm spoken to, I listen.", "author": "Chance Garton", "portrait": "https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/5987d897cf81e0278ec5322e/aa717e55-9487-4255-a7df-3f8ef10940c4/Chance+Garton+Patreon+Portrait.png?content-type=image%2Fpng"}, {"text": "Instead of going for the big procedure that's expensive and has this cascade of effects that comes after it, can we just try this one thing and see how that goes?", "author": "Kyle Denton", "portrait": "https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/5987d897cf81e0278ec5322e/3bfe296c-3dcd-4af6-bc2e-26466a87ec04/KYLE-DENTON.png?content-type=image%2Fpng"}, {"text": "We need to solve this in a way that we don't deal with it again and move on, versus, \"It's okay if you keep coming back to me forever and keep paying me.\"", "author": "Chance Garton", "portrait": "https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/5987d897cf81e0278ec5322e/aa717e55-9487-4255-a7df-3f8ef10940c4/Chance+Garton+Patreon+Portrait.png?content-type=image%2Fpng"}, {"text": "48% of Americans have some form, whether it's gingivitis or periodontitis. So are we expected to believe that half of the population isn't taking care of their teeth according to the standards of the dentist?", "author": "Kyle Denton", "portrait": "https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/5987d897cf81e0278ec5322e/3bfe296c-3dcd-4af6-bc2e-26466a87ec04/KYLE-DENTON.png?content-type=image%2Fpng"}, {"text": "I think a lot of jaw tension, as a matter of fact, is the stress between these two polarities of thought and emotion.", "author": "Kyle Denton", "portrait": "https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/5987d897cf81e0278ec5322e/3bfe296c-3dcd-4af6-bc2e-26466a87ec04/KYLE-DENTON.png?content-type=image%2Fpng"}]
fields.Quotes JSON: [{"text": "I am worthy of taking care of myself. I take care of myself and I accept this time to do so so that I could take care of everything else.", "author": "Kyle Denton", "portrait": "https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/5987d897cf81e0278ec5322e/3bfe296c-3dcd-4af6-bc2e-26466a87ec04/KYLE-DENTON.png?content-type=image%2Fpng"}, {"text": "In all of the areas of terrain health or holistic health, what have you, I think the tooth situation is the one that is most poorly represented.", "author": "Chance Garton", "portrait": "https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/5987d897cf81e0278ec5322e/aa717e55-9487-4255-a7df-3f8ef10940c4/Chance+Garton+Patreon+Portrait.png?content-type=image%2Fpng"}, {"text": "The best way to help our teeth is really to help our body internally recognize the signals of fight or flight, rest and relax.", "author": "Kyle Denton", "portrait": "https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/5987d897cf81e0278ec5322e/3bfe296c-3dcd-4af6-bc2e-26466a87ec04/KYLE-DENTON.png?content-type=image%2Fpng"}, {"text": "We're not approaching healing to fix brokenness. We're approaching healing as an expression of innate wholeness.", "author": "Chance Garton", "portrait": "https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/5987d897cf81e0278ec5322e/aa717e55-9487-4255-a7df-3f8ef10940c4/Chance+Garton+Patreon+Portrait.png?content-type=image%2Fpng"}, {"text": "Sometimes when we're faced with something like a toothache, which doesn't give us a break, even a crying child can give you a break, but a toothache is just like every heartbeat.", "author": "Kyle Denton", "portrait": "https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/5987d897cf81e0278ec5322e/3bfe296c-3dcd-4af6-bc2e-26466a87ec04/KYLE-DENTON.png?content-type=image%2Fpng"}, {"text": "And then there's the underwriters, the real puppet string holders of the insurance companies that really have a lot of say in how a dentist will perform and work.", "author": "Kyle Denton", "portrait": "https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/5987d897cf81e0278ec5322e/3bfe296c-3dcd-4af6-bc2e-26466a87ec04/KYLE-DENTON.png?content-type=image%2Fpng"}, {"text": "Don't be afraid to ask more questions or to just kick the can down the road if it's clearly not an emergency.", "author": "Chance Garton", "portrait": "https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/5987d897cf81e0278ec5322e/aa717e55-9487-4255-a7df-3f8ef10940c4/Chance+Garton+Patreon+Portrait.png?content-type=image%2Fpng"}, {"text": "With any type of doctor, just consider everything an offer. Everything's an offer. It's on the table.", "author": "Kyle Denton", "portrait": "https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/5987d897cf81e0278ec5322e/3bfe296c-3dcd-4af6-bc2e-26466a87ec04/KYLE-DENTON.png?content-type=image%2Fpng"}]
